_doc: FP viewmodel export contract. One entry per gun that ships clips. Names are API (research doc production/research/blender_godot_fp_pipeline_2026-07-25.md section 2.3): renaming an object, marker or NLA track here or in the .blend is a breaking change. Driver: tools/export_all_viewmodels.py. Validator: tools/validate_viewmodel_glb.py. Godot-side probe: tests/test_viewmodel_contract.tscn. Gameplay timers in weapon_tres are kept equal to the authored clip lengths by tools/sync_weapon_timers.py, which the export driver runs; validate_viewmodel_glb.py --check-timers fails on drift.
_contacts_doc: Marker/rail contract (war_room/2026-07-27_viewmodel_pipeline_v2): 'contacts' maps a contact-marker empty to the part it is parented to. A hand that manipulates a part is posed TO its marker, never eyeballed in free space; sliding parts keep origin-at-home 1-DOF rails. tools/audit_viewmodel_rigs.py measures hand-to-marker closest approach per clip and flags a reach that never closes to a true grab (FAKED IN AIR).
_staged_doc: 2026-07-27 transplant (tools/transplant_armory_parts.py): every fused gun copy replaced by its armory assembly with split moving parts + contact markers. When a gun below joins 'guns', move its entry's contacts map in and declare its parts. Rails clamped where travel is recorded: Ithaca37_pump x[0,0.045], M72_LAW_inner_tube x[0,0.230].

_items_doc: NON-GUN FP ITEMS. Same export driver and same validator as `guns`, three differences: the root key is `item_root` not `gun_root`; `markers` names its own required empties instead of the SightRear/SightFront/MuzzlePoint iron-sight set (`markers_under_gun` is FALSE - these are not guns and have no sights); and no `weapon_tres`, so sync_weapon_timers.py never runs against them. EVERYTHING ELSE IS THE SAME LAW: the clip set must match EXACTLY (no extras), and EVERY clip must carry a channel for EVERY listed part. VOCABULARY, and the names are the ENGINE's not the item's: `rifle_idle` = the held pose (weapon_holder.gd:934 asks for this literal string on EVERY viewmodel, gun or not - an idle named anything else plays NOTHING and renders in bind pose); `charge_handle` = the DRAW (weapon_holder.gd:939 auto-plays it on equip, so the CS-style deploy is free); `fire` = the item's action. There is NO `equip` and NO `holster` - SPEC.md asks for both and is wrong; nothing plays on holster anywhere in this engine, so a holster clip needs new code, not new art. The grenade is the one item with an extra action (`throw`), because cook-and-hold then release is two beats of gameplay that one `fire` cannot express. Playback for all of these is scripts/weapons/item_viewmodel.gd. Borrow map from the CC0 stock arm clips: production/research/equipment_viewmodels/STOCK_CLIP_SOURCES.md.

handset._note: AUTHORED 2026-07-30. Names here now match the blend (they were placeholders). rifle_idle = 91f loop held at the Godot placeholder spot (player.gd:348 position 0.16,-0.14,-0.32 = right 160 / down 140 / fwd 320 from the eye), fingers flexing ~10mm. charge_handle = 32f: up from below, through Caleb's at-ear pose at f15 (pose_library/radio_at_ear.json), hold, then settle onto the idle at f32 (handoff measured 0.000mm). Radio_Handset_root is CHILD_OF ArmsRig_Radio_Handset/hand.R - the exporter bakes that to TRS, glTF carries no constraints. Replaces the BoxMesh at player.gd:339.

claymore._note: fire = the two-handed plant (borrow push.L/push.R). face_Claymore +Y is the kill direction (Blender +Y = Godot -Z). grip_R_Claymore was flagged a GUESS - confirm before export. Model is 128mm wide vs a real M18's 216mm.

m26_grenade._note: charge_handle = draw (grab.R), fire = PIN PULL (grab.L), throw = the release (jab.R). Splitting M26_pin is what lets the pin actually leave. The throw's release frame must line up with grenade_handler.throw() spawning the projectile.

bandage._note: fire = the wrap (borrow finger_gun_fix, the only two-handed fiddling clip). Stretched to HealthSystem._heal_time_this at runtime, so author it at any comfortable length.

knife._note: The stock CC0 set IS the knife's clip set, no retarget: knife_draw -> charge_handle, knife_idle -> rifle_idle, knife_hit_01 -> fire. MeleeVerb decides lethality, not the clip.
